families.note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-25 (dated from the newest rows in the recorder's own store, not from this machine's clock, which reads two different days depending which setting is asked). WHAT THE LANE DOES: a factory or data centre's grid bill for a whole year is largely set by how much it was pulling during a handful of hours -- the hours when the whole grid was at its busiest. Once a day, for the day after, the recorder reads the grid operator's own published forecast and writes down one of two things: cut your load, or ordinary day. That is a call. It is sealed with a fingerprint at the moment it is made, before anyone knows how the day went, and it is scored afterwards against the operator's own record of what actually happened -- wrong calls included, one row per call. NOTHING HAS EVER BEEN SOLD HERE and there is no price on the page. The lane's own spec describes a possible paid product later (the calls themselves, ahead of the day) but that is a separate decision that has not been made, and the recorder's own can_we_sell() answers no and names the reasons. The page is the free scoreboard, and it is free forever: the whole record is on it. NO SAMPLE FILE, ON PURPOSE, AND sample_status IS 'fail' RATHER THAN 'on-page' FOR A REASON. There is no file behind this page to slice, so there is nothing to sample and the pill saying 'sample not ready' is correct. It is NOT 'on-page' either: on-page means the whole of what we hold is printed on the page, and that is false here -- the page prints every call, but the recorded grid load behind the threshold rule (hundreds of days of it) is counted on the page, not printed on it. Calling it on-page would be a sentence a stranger could check and find untrue. THERE IS NO UPLOAD SERVICE, no form, no account and no self-serve anything -- this estate's platform is not ours to add one to. The only way in is an email thread with a person, which is what the contact block on the page says. NO NUMBER, DATE, PRICE, GROUP, CADENCE OR BUYER IS TYPED INTO THE PAGE. scripts/slice_peak_call.py reads group, cadence, buyer and price out of this row with no fallback, and reads every call, date, hour, megawatt figure, fingerprint and count out of revenue-2026/var/peak_call.db read-only at build time. It recomputes every call's fingerprint with the recorder's own function on every build and refuses to write the page if one no longer matches, because the only claim this record makes is that it was not edited after the fact. It also reads the addresses the recorder fetches out of the recorder's own code and refuses to build unless each one carries a permission note whose verdict is 'allowed' -- a grid operator that refuses to be read is never named here as a source of anything. THE ZEROS ARE THE CONTENT, NOT A GAP. At 2026-08-25 no call had been scored yet and no call had told anyone to cut, and the page says both in words rather than printing an empty counter. The recorder's own written bar refuses a hit rate under 5 warnings, and refuses to call the record sellable under 60 scored calls, 5 warnings and 90 days of public record -- all three written down on 2026-08-24 while the answer to all three was still no. The page carries that bar and no percentage. cadence_long is NOT stored in this row on purpose: the module recounts it off the sealed calls at build time, so the page cannot go stale even if this row does. STILL TO WIRE, FOR WHOEVER MERGES THIS: there is no peak-call entry in scripts/family_status.py. The day this row is merged into catalog.json it stops being harmless: the built page will carry no read-date stamp and scripts/check_built.py will mark it as a page with no read date. The store is at an absolute path, which _store_path() already supports. CORRECTION 2026-08-25, appended not edited: this row was written as sample_status "fail" and that was the wrong word. "fail" means a sample file exists and is wrong; there is no sample file here and there is never going to be one, because the record on the page IS the product. The page said both "sample not ready" and "all of it is on the page" in the same paragraph, which are the two halves of a contradiction — a stranger reads "sample not ready" as a file that is coming, and no file is coming. NOBODY IS ON IT, and that is not a build failure -- it is the lane refusing itself. Two separate written permissions have to be in place before one name can appear and only one of them is. The operator's dated decision at revenue-2026/approvals/read_public_sites.md reads `status: ACTIVE`, `approved_on: 2026-08-25`, and it answers ONE question: may a machine of ours read other companies' public websites at all. It does not answer the second question a table about named businesses cannot publish without -- WHO IS ON THE TABLE, and where that list of names came from. OPERATOR DECISION NEEDED: which shop list, and somebody reading that source's terms on a named day and writing down what they said. Nothing in this build may write that declaration, because a machine that can declare its own list source has no list source. NO SHOP, NO PERSON AND NO PRICE IS NAMED ANYWHERE ON THE PAGE. Nothing has ever been sold here: the lane's sales table holds no rows, read read-only as the page was built, and the catalog price stays 'Not for sale yet'. The lane's code carries two prices for the paid evidence report and neither is printed on this page, because a price on the page is a promise this build has no authority to make. WHAT THE PAGE PRINTS IS THE LANE'S OWN PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, WORD FOR WORD, NOT A DESCRIPTION OF IT: revenue-2026/var/agent_ready_data.db holds one render, state `published`, `on_day: 2026-08-25`, and scripts/slice_agent_ready.py RE-CHECKS THAT DOCUMENT'S FINGERPRINT with the lane's own hashing function before printing a character of it -- a document whose stored fingerprint no longer matches its stored text stops the build. Every date on the page is read off a dated row or a dated file in that way; not one is taken from this machine's clock, which reads two different days depending on the setting. SAMPLE STATUS IS on-page AND IT IS ENFORCED, NOT ASSERTED: every table in the lane's store is empty except the one holding that published document, so there is no file to sample and the page IS the whole of what we hold. The slicer reads the store read-only on every build and REFUSES TO BUILD if a row appears in any table other than the renders table, because 'the whole of what we hold is printed on this page' stops being true the moment a shop is listed. THE LANE'S OWN WORDING GUARD IS RUN AGAIN AT PAGE-BUILD TIME AND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the published document must clear projects/agent_ready/row.wording_problems(), and a line assembled out of that guard's own first banned phrase must be refused -- a guard nobody has seen say no is a decoration.
